title: The Importance of Congregational Prayer
excerpt: Understanding the significance of praying in congregation and its rewards.
content:
The congregational prayer (Salat al-Jama'ah) holds great significance in Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said: "The prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times superior to the prayer offered by a person alone."

Praying in congregation brings numerous benefits:

1. Spiritual rewards multiplied 27 times
2. Unity and brotherhood among Muslims
3. Regular connection with the community
4. Accountability and mutual support
5. Following the Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH)

At Minhaajulhudaa Masjid, we encourage all community members to attend congregational prayers, especially Fajr and Isha. The masjid is open for all five daily prayers.

title: Preparing for Ramadan: A Complete Guide
excerpt: Practical tips to prepare spiritually, physically, and mentally for the blessed month.
content:
Ramadan is a month of immense blessings and spiritual growth. Proper preparation helps us make the most of this sacred month.

## Spiritual Preparation
- Increase your voluntary prayers
- Start fasting on Mondays and Thursdays
- Increase Qur'an recitation
- Make tawbah and mend relationships

## Physical Preparation
- Adjust your sleep schedule
- Reduce caffeine gradually
- Plan your meals for Suhoor and Iftar
- Stay hydrated

## Mental Preparation
- Set clear Ramadan goals
- Plan your daily schedule
- Limit social media usage
- Prepare a reading list

## Community Preparation
- Volunteer at the masjid
- Plan charity activities
- Prepare for Taraweeh prayers
- Reach out to family and friends

May Allah allow us to reach Ramadan and accept our worship.

title: Understanding Zakat: The Third Pillar
excerpt: A comprehensive guide to calculating and paying Zakat correctly.
content:
Zakat is the obligatory annual charity that every adult, sane Muslim who possesses wealth above the Nisab must pay. It is 2.5% of accumulated wealth held for one lunar year.

## Who Must Pay Zakat?
- Adult Muslims
- Sane individuals
- Those whose wealth exceeds the Nisab
- Wealth held for one full lunar year

## What is Nisab?
The Nisab is the minimum amount of wealth a Muslim must own before Zakat becomes obligatory. It is equivalent to 85 grams of gold or 595 grams of silver.

## What is Zakatable?
- Cash and savings
- Gold and silver
- Business inventory
- Agricultural produce
- Livestock
- Investments and stocks

## How to Calculate?
Zakat = 2.5% of total zakatable wealth after deducting immediate debts and expenses.

If you need help calculating your Zakat, please visit the masjid office. Our team can assist you.
